text:
sara_support: FYI customer (Acme SRE) opened a P1 — long-running generation gets cut off at ~30s when using our Python SDK. They say they set an env var but still hit a client-side cutoff. Repro steps below.

jordan_eng: Can you paste the exact env and client config? often an env var vs client arg mismatch.

sara_support: They provided this: `export REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30` and the app calls `client = RedwoodClient(timeout=120)` in python. SDK version `0.9.3`. Customer says streaming tokens stop and SDK raises `ReadTimeout`.

jordan_eng: Hmm. SDK 0.9.x used `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS` internally for env var in one release (bug) — mixing seconds vs ms has bitten us. Also older SDKs interpret `timeout` tuple differently (connect, read) vs single deadline. Need logs.

sara_support: Attached logs (redacted): `2024-10-03T14:22:51Z ERROR read timeout after 30s stream aborted` then `client closed connection`. They reported seeing HTTP 499 at our LB + a 200-ish partial response upstream.

jordan_eng: 499 suggests client closed the connection. If env var is 30 (interpreted as ms) but client arg is 120s, the env var might override runtime in the older SDK. Also proxies like CloudFront/ALB can have idle timeouts ~30s. Two layers to check: SDK-level read deadline and infra idle timeouts.

devops_anna: We also saw recent ALB timeouts bumped to 30s in the staging rule set accidentally. I'll check their account region for custom NGW values.

mike_prod: Customer mentioned unexpected duplicate billing when SDK retried. If the SDK retries on timeout, they might be charged twice for partial token output. Need to confirm retry policy for streaming aborts in 0.9.3.

jordan_eng: In 0.9.x the default retry on idempotent requests only — streaming is non-idempotent, but we had a bug where some timeouts triggered the retry path. That was fixed in 1.1.x. Recommend upgrading.

sara_support: Customer is on pinned Docker image. They wanted a workaround first. Any suggestion we can tell them to try now?

jordan_eng: Quick mitigations: 1) set env `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS=120000` (explicit ms) or export `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=120` only if using SDK >=1.x. 2) Pass explicit `timeout=(10, 300)` on the `requests`-style client if they use a tuple semantics — example:
```python
client = RedwoodClient(timeout=(10, 600))  # connect 10s, read 600s
# or deadline-style in newer SDKs:
client = RedwoodClient(timeout=600)
```
3) Disable automatic retries for streaming: `client = RedwoodClient(retries=0)` or set `RETRY_MODE=off` env while they test. 4) Verify ALB/NGW idle timeout > generation time.

devops_anna: Confirmed: their account had an ALB idle timeout set to 30s in the manifest for legacy stacks. I'll raise it to 600s for them temporarily.

sara_support: I sent that checklist and asked them to try upgrade to `redwood==1.1.2` and set `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS=120000`. They said they can test tomorrow and asked if we can reproduce internally.

jordan_eng: I pushed a small repro script to my laptop and ran a streaming long-gen (80s). On 0.9.3 with `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30` I saw the client abort at ~30s; on 1.1.2 with `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS=120000` it stayed open. I'll capture logs and sample requests.

jordan_eng: repro snippet I used:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"redacted\", timeout=(5, 300), retries=0)
resp = client.generate_stream(model=\"gpt-large\", prompt=\"long output test\n\"*1000)
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text, end='')
```

sara_support: Please drop your internal logs here when ready. I'll keep the ticket updated and coordinate with Acme. :thumbsup:

mike_prod: Also add a short note to the docs about env var names/units and a migration note for 0.9 -> 1.x. This will reduce future confusion.

jordan_eng: Agreed. I'll open a docs PR referencing the migration gotcha and add a small test to catch env-unit regressions.

deploy_bot: Deployment scheduled: ALB timeout change (staging->prod) for account acme-corp at 2024-10-04T03:00:00Z, change-id 4572.
